advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the behavioural test assert Resolved-vs-active classification against the production compute_snapshot output (or the two production query results captured via client.search_calls), not by re-invoking the fake directly on freshly-built JQL.
evidence: `active_hits = {i["key"] for i in client.search_issues(active_jql)}` (line 400) — assertion re-invokes the fake directly, not compute_snapshot output
`assert {"REB-1", "REB-2"} <= set(snapshot)` (line 409) — the sole snapshot-level assertion; passes under old literal-status code too since both queries combined return both issues

`snapshot[key] = {k: fields[k] for k in sorted(fields.keys())}` (fetcher.py:594) — the snapshot is a flat key->fields dict that does not record which query (active vs done) surfaced each issue, so active/done classification is not observable from the returned snapshot
advisory.finding: The behavioural test's only assertion against the production compute_snapshot output (line 409, `{"REB-1","REB-2"} <= set(snapshot)`) is regression-blind: under the old literal `status != "Done"` code both the Resolved and In-Progress issues still land in the merged snapshot (the union of the active + done queries), so this assertion passes both before and after the fix. The discriminating assertions (lines 399-406) do NOT read the snapshot — they re-invoke `client.search_issues(active_jql)`/`(done_jql)` directly on the test's own fake, so they verify the builder strings + the fake's self-authored `_matches` logic rather than the production classification through `_build_snapshot`.
scenarios: A future regression reverting jql builders to literal `status` while leaving the merge intact would still pass line 409 (both issues present), so the test named as the behavioural oracle would not fail on the merge path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert on `client.search_calls` (which records the JQLs the production _build_snapshot actually issued) and/or on a snapshot representation that distinguishes active from done, so the oracle fails when classification regresses through the real merge path rather than only when the builder string changes.
